## Summary

- **The pitch:** timed to a red crypto day — a vault that "just had one of its best days" precisely because the market bled. The strategy family is named in the title: positive convexity, i.e. long-gamma-like exposure — accelerating gains in large moves, slow bleed in calm or chop. The manager's own framing is the honest part: "most of the time it slowly bleeds. This vault yearns for chaos."
- **Mechanics (tweet + vault page):** BTC only; rebalances daily; trades perpetual futures on Hyperliquid (page: "Strategies used by vault: Perpetual futures"); lockup 1 day; fees 10% performance / 0% management / 0% deposit-withdrawal.

## Why it matters

- **This is the mirror image of the Astraeus arc — the two vaults monetize opposite regimes.** The torn-down FM vault sells crash premium: it absorbs forced dips, "gets paid for providing liquidity when nobody else wants to", and needed manual rescue buys when June turned chaotic ([[2026-11-11-astraeus-hl-vault-reverse-engineering]], [[2026-11-11-fmchain-vault-owner-response]]). +convexity holds the other side of that trade: it pays on the days the dip-absorber blows up, and bleeds on the calm days the dip-absorber harvests. Held together they approximate owning both tails; held separately, each is an explicit bet on which premium is mispriced. The Astraeus teardown already documented that the short-gamma premium is decaying — the open question this vault poses is whether the long-gamma side is correspondingly cheap.
- **Sharpe is the wrong yardstick here, and the tweet accidentally says so.** A 1.6 lifetime Sharpe with -12.2% max DD looks mediocre until you notice the return shape: a few vertical days carrying long flat-bleed stretches. The correct metric for a long-convexity book is tail-capture per unit of bleed — how much of each crash day it converts, versus what the carry costs between crashes. The page's own window table shows the profile: 13.4% in the crash month vs slow singles otherwise.
- **Skepticism gates:** the author is the platform promoting a listing on its own directory (the tweet IS the marketing); the headline rank (#1 week) is recency-bait measured over exactly the regime the strategy needs, while lifetime sits at #36; 1.2 years of history is roughly one chaos cycle — the "few good days" sample is tiny; $1.2M TVL means capacity and unwind questions; the CCC protocol rating with ~48% modeled probability-of-loss prices in a real chance the venue itself fails regardless of strategy quality; and every performance number comes from the promoter's own cleaned PnL methodology.
- **Actionable:** light task filed — decide whether this one is worth tracking as the chaos complement to the Astraeus arc. Watch-not-act framing: trading decisions live in the other company; this is second-brain material.
